Barnstable.metaTitle: Wildlife Removal in Barnstable, MA | Cape Cod Pros
Barnstable.metaDescription: Bats, raccoons, and squirrels removed in Barnstable, MA — from Hyannis Harbor to Sandy Neck. Seasonal-home specialists, same-day service from our crew. Call us today.
Barnstable.housing_era: The town mixes full-time Cape cottages and ranches in Marstons Mills and West Barnstable with dense year-round housing around Hyannis and a very large stock of seasonal homes in Osterville, Cotuit, and Centerville that sit closed through the winter.
Barnstable.geographic_features: Cape Cod Bay (Sandy Neck barrier beach on the north side), Hyannis Harbor (busy ferry and fishing harbor on Nantucket Sound), Lake Wequaquet (largest freshwater pond on Cape Cod), Centerville River (tidal river through Centerville and Osterville)

Barnstable.wildlife_intro:
Barnstable is the Cape's largest town, and its wildlife calls follow its split personality: busy year-round neighborhoods around Hyannis and quiet seasonal villages that empty out after summer. Raccoons work chimneys and soffits in Hyannis and Marstons Mills, gray squirrels chew into attics under the oak canopy, and bats settle into the eaves and attics of Osterville, Cotuit, and Centerville houses that sit closed for months. Skunks den under porches and sheds, and rats turn up around the harbor and restaurant blocks.

Spring opening is our busiest season here. Homeowners unlocking a house after winter often find bat colonies, squirrel nests, or a winter's worth of mice, and our crew can inspect the whole roofline and seal entry points in one visit. In summer we handle raccoon families, skunk dens, and bats in active homes, always working as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent and scheduling bat exclusion inside the permitted spring and late-summer windows. Call us and we will get out the same day.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Barnstable?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how many entry points need sealing, so we inspect first and explain the full scope and price before any work begins. Seasonal homes with a long-standing bat colony or squirrel damage usually take more work than a single raccoon in a chimney. Call us for an inspection and a clear, no-pressure quote.

faqs.q: We just opened our Osterville house and found bats in the attic. What happens now?
faqs.a: Do not seal anything yet — bats in Massachusetts are handled by exclusion only, and eviction is only permitted May 1 to May 31 or August 1 to October 15 under PAC permit conditions, so pups are never trapped inside. Our crew confirms the species and entry points, then installs one-way exits in the legal window and seals the house once the colony has left.

Falmouth.wildlife_intro:
Falmouth's mix of year-round neighborhoods and south-shore seasonal homes keeps our crew busy in every season. Bats roost in the attics of older homes in Falmouth village and Woods Hole, raccoons raid chimneys and trash near the harbors, and gray squirrels are constant in the oak and pine woods behind East Falmouth's subdivisions. Skunks dig under porches in West and North Falmouth, and mice and rats move into closed-up cottages around Waquoit Bay as the weather turns cold.

The signature Falmouth job is the spring opening: a house shuttered since September gets unlocked to find droppings in the attic, a squirrel nest in the soffit, or a raccoon that spent the winter in the chimney. Our crew inspects, removes what is there under Massachusetts PAC rules, and seals the openings so the house stays clear all summer. Summer calls lean toward raccoon families, skunks under decks, and bats discovered in occupied homes. Call us for same-day help anywhere in town.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Falmouth?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the species involved, the size of the job, and how much exclusion and cleanup the house needs, which is why we start with an inspection. A single skunk den is a different job from a bat colony in a seasonal home that has been closed all winter. We explain everything up front before work starts — call us to schedule.

faqs.q: Why do we keep getting mice in our Waquoit cottage every winter?
faqs.a: Closed seasonal homes are easy targets: no people, no noise, and small gaps at the foundation, bulkhead, and roofline that white-footed mice only need a pencil-width opening to use. Once inside they nest in wall voids and stored linens. Our crew finds and seals those entry points with chew-resistant materials and clears the animals already inside, which is what stops the yearly repeat.

Yarmouth.wildlife_intro:
Yarmouth runs bay to sound, and the wildlife changes with the shoreline. Along Route 6A in Yarmouth Port, bats and squirrels get into the attics of sea captains' houses with old chimneys and layered rooflines. In South and West Yarmouth, raccoons work the cottage colonies and year-round neighborhoods, skunks den under porches and rental decks, and rats follow the Route 28 restaurant and motel corridor. The Bass River marshes and the town's kettle ponds keep mosquitoes aside, the real pressure is structural: older roofs, vent gaps, and crawl spaces.

Like the rest of the Mid Cape, Yarmouth's seasonal homes drive a spring surge — cottages opened in April and May reveal bat colonies and overwintering squirrels that moved in months earlier. Our crew handles those cleanouts, seals the entry points, and stays available through summer for raccoon families and skunk dens in occupied homes. We work as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent, and bat evictions are timed to the permitted May and August-to-October windows. Call us for same-day service.

faqs.q: How much will wildlife removal cost at my Yarmouth home?
faqs.a: Cost follows the job: the animal, the access it used, and whether attic cleanup or multi-point sealing is needed. We inspect the property first, show you exactly what we found, and quote the complete job before starting. That inspection-first approach applies to a Yarmouth Port captain's house or a West Yarmouth cottage alike — call us to book one.

faqs.q: Are the bats in my Route 6A attic protected?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts bats are protected, and removal means exclusion only — never trapping or killing. Eviction is allowed only from May 1 to May 31 or August 1 to October 15 under PAC permit conditions, so flightless pups are not separated from the colony. Our crew installs one-way exits during a legal window, then seals every gap once the bats have left for good.

Bourne.wildlife_intro:
Bourne is where the Cape begins, and the Cape Cod Canal shapes its wildlife. The canal's wooded banks and the Buzzards Bay shoreline give raccoons, skunks, and opossums easy travel routes into Pocasset, Cataumet, and Monument Beach neighborhoods. Bats roost in the attics of canal-era homes in Buzzards Bay and in seasonal cottages that sit empty all winter, gray squirrels work the oak woods behind Sagamore's subdivisions, and rats are a steady issue around the canal-side commercial blocks.

Spring brings the familiar Upper Cape pattern: seasonal homes opened to bat droppings, squirrel nests, and mouse damage from the quiet months. Our crew clears the animals, seals the roofline and foundation gaps, and can check a second property while we are in town. Summer work is raccoon families in chimneys, skunks under shore-cottage porches, and the occasional beaver flooding complaint on the Pocasset River, which we handle within the permit process Massachusetts requires. Call us — same-day service across Bourne.

faqs.q: What does it cost to get wildlife out of a Bourne home?
faqs.a: Every property is different, so cost depends on the species, the number of entry points, and whether cleanup is needed after the animals are out. We inspect first and give you the full price for removal, sealing, and cleanup before any work begins — no surprises afterward. Call us to arrange an inspection at your home.

faqs.q: A beaver keeps flooding our road near the Pocasset River. Can you help?
faqs.a: Beaver flooding in Massachusetts is permit-framed work. Outside the regular trapping season, beaver problems that threaten health or safety go through a Board of Health emergency permit, and our crew can assess the site, explain the permit path, and carry out the permitted work, which may include flow devices or dam breaching where allowed.

Dennis.wildlife_intro:
Dennis stretches from Sesuit Harbor to the Bass River, and its housing — captains' houses on Route 6A, cottage colonies in Dennis Port, and subdivisions in South Dennis — gives wildlife plenty of ways in. Bats settle into the attics of older East Dennis and Dennis Village homes, gray squirrels work the tree canopy over South Dennis, and raccoons are constant around the harbor, the river marinas, and the trash areas behind seasonal cottages. Skunks den under porches in West Dennis, and rats appear around the Route 28 food businesses.

The Dennis calendar is driven by the cottage season. Spring openings reveal bats, squirrels, and mice that wintered in closed cottages; fall closings are when owners ask our crew to seal everything before the empty months. Summer brings raccoon families and skunk calls from occupied rentals and homes. As a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent, we handle bat exclusion only inside the permitted May and August-to-October windows and seal entry points so colonies cannot return. Call us for same-day help.

faqs.q: What will wildlife removal cost at my Dennis cottage?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, the size of the cottage colony or nest, and how much sealing the building needs — cottage roofs often have more than one gap. We inspect first, explain the work in plain terms, and give you the full price before we start. Call us to book an inspection before or after the season.

faqs.q: Shorebirds nest near our Dennis Port beach house. Will you remove them?

What our crew can do is help with the animals that are legal to address around a beach house: raccoons in the attic, skunks under the porch, and deterrence for pigeons, starlings, and house sparrows nesting in vents and eaves.
